findings.description:
ICE PACK TEST

INDICATION: Evaluation of bilateral ptosis, right greater than left.

TECHNIQUE: Crushed ice in a surgical glove applied over the closed right upper eyelid for 2 minutes. Marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) measured immediately before and after application.

RESULTS:
  Right MRD1 before application: 0.5 mm.
  Right MRD1 after application (2 minutes): 3.0 mm.
  Improvement: 2.5 mm.

IMPRESSION: Positive ice pack test (improvement in ptosis of at least 2 mm after cooling). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Positive ice pack test: right MRD1 improved from 0.5 mm to 3.0 mm (2.5 mm) after 2 minutes of cooling

findings.description:
BEDSIDE RESPIRATORY FUNCTION TESTING

INDICATION: Generalized fatigable weakness with bulbar symptoms; baseline respiratory muscle strength.

MEASUREMENTS (seated; weight 54.8 kg, height 160 cm):
  FVC: 2.95 L (predicted 3.25 L; 91% predicted; 54 mL/kg)
  MIP (NIF): -58 cmH2O (lower limit of normal for age and sex about -55 cmH2O)
  MEP: 76 cmH2O (lower limit of normal about 70 cmH2O)
  Single-breath count: 34
  Cough: strong

IMPRESSION: FVC, MIP and MEP within the predicted range. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: FVC 2.95 L (91% predicted, 54 mL/kg), MIP -58 cmH2O, MEP 76 cmH2O: within the predicted range

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 5.8 nmol/L (reference <= 0.02) with blocking 58% and modulating 74%; TSH 1.9, free T4 and anti-TPO normal; anti-GAD65 > 2000 IU/mL
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable bilateral ptosis, diplopia, bulbar and proximal weakness: AChR binding antibody (RIA or cell-based assay) first, with thyroid function because autoimmune thyroid disease clusters with MG and type 1 diabetes (Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019; Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 3 Hz decrement in deltoid 17% and nasalis 20% with normal baseline CMAPs, no post-exercise facilitation (3%) and normal nerve conductions
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz in facial and proximal muscles
action_criteria.rationale: Low-rate RNS of weak facial and proximal muscles documents the postsynaptic decrement; brief exercise testing excludes presynaptic facilitation, and nerve conductions exclude a diabetic neuropathy (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Orbicularis oculi mean MCD 71 microseconds with increased jitter in 16 of 20 pairs and blocking in 7
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG (not needed once RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: SFEMG is reserved for a normal RNS or seronegative disease; with positive AChR antibodies and a clear decrement it adds nothing to the diagnosis (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right MRD1 improves from 0.5 to 3.0 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Bedside ice pack test of the right ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable bilateral ptosis, worse on the right: an MRD1 improvement of at least 2 mm after cooling is cheap bedside support for a neuromuscular junction disorder.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No anterior mediastinal mass; fatty thymic involution appropriate for age; no thymoma
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the mediastinum for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Mediastinal imaging is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025); without thymoma she is a candidate for thymectomy under the MGTX criteria.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 2.95 L (91% predicted, 54 mL/kg), MIP -58 cmH2O, MEP 76 cmH2O: no respiratory compromise
action_criteria.label: Measure FVC, MIP and MEP as a respiratory baseline
action_criteria.rationale: Dysphagia, nasal speech and neck flexor weakness: FVC in mL/kg, MIP and MEP give the baseline before immunotherapy and thymectomy (20/30/40 rule, Lawn, Arch Neurol 2001).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No pyridostigmine interaction; steroid-induced rise in insulin requirement; avoid codeine
action_criteria.label: Check the planned MG treatment against her insulin and codeine intolerance
action_criteria.rationale: No interaction changes the choice of drug; prednisone will raise her insulin requirement and codeine is documented as not tolerated.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to stiff-person syndrome, a diabetic cranial neuropathy or a functional cause before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily and titrate to 60 mg four to five times daily according to response and gastrointestinal muscarinic side effects

Start prednisone at 10-20 mg/day and increase gradually with monitoring of bulbar and respiratory function for early steroid-induced worsening; add a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) if long-term steroids are needed
Plan insulin pump adjustment with the diabetes team when prednisone starts: frequent capillary glucose monitoring and increased basal and bolus insulin for steroid-induced hyperglycaemia

Refer for elective thymectomy once symptoms are controlled: thymectomy is recommended for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65 (MGTX); give IVIG or plasma exchange before surgery if bulbar weakness persists
Do not prescribe codeine (documented intolerance); use any opioid cautiously because of respiratory depression in MG
Record the very high anti-GAD65 titre and reassess for a GAD-associated neurological syndrome if rigidity, spasms or ataxia appear
Give her a list of drugs that can worsen MG and check every new prescription against it

avoided_actions.rationale: MG is a disorder of the neuromuscular junction; EEG has no diagnostic role (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in MG; without rigidity, spasms, ataxia or a CNS sign the anti-GAD65 titre does not call for CSF studies (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
FDG-PET has no role in MG; mediastinal CT answers the thymoma question (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
Brain and orbit MRI is reserved for negative serology and neurophysiology or a central or orbital mimic; here AChR antibodies and RNS are positive (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
No cardiac symptom or sign; echocardiography is not part of the MG work-up.
Regular rhythm and no palpitations or syncope; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), AChR antibody-positive, without thymoma; concurrent type 1 diabetes with markedly elevated anti-GAD65 (polyautoimmunity)

differential.key_features: Anti-GAD65 > 2000 IU/mL is in the range seen in GAD-associated neurological syndromes, but she has no axial or limb rigidity, spasms or exaggerated startle; fatigable ptosis, diplopia and bulbar weakness with AChR antibodies and a decrement are MG.
A diabetic cranial mononeuropathy is acute, usually painful and fixed; here the ptosis is bilateral and fatigable, the right adduction deficit fluctuates, and bulbar and limb muscles fatigue too.
Normal baseline CMAPs, a 3 Hz decrement and no post-exercise facilitation (3%), preserved reflexes, prominent ocular signs; AChR binding antibody strongly positive.
Patient not on penicillamine or other MG-inducing agents.
Markedly positive AChR establishes organic pathology.

key_clinical_evidence: Fluctuating, fatigable weakness with a diurnal pattern (worse in the evening) is the clinical hallmark of MG; fixed weakness suggests an alternative diagnosis.
Ocular involvement (ptosis, diplopia) is asymmetric and fatigable in MG; thyroid eye disease causes restrictive, not fatigable, ophthalmoplegia.
AChR binding antibody 5.8 nmol/L with a 17-20% decrement on 3 Hz RNS establishes generalized AChR-positive MG; SFEMG is not needed.

Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma; here it is normal, and thymectomy is still recommended under MGTX for non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
Fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium and neuromuscular blockers can worsen MG and must be checked against every new prescription.

Polyautoimmunity: MG with type 1 diabetes. The very high anti-GAD65 titre is more typical of GAD-associated neurological syndromes than of diabetes alone, but without rigidity, spasms or ataxia it does not explain fatigable ocular and bulbar weakness.
Prednisone will raise her insulin requirement; the pump settings must be adjusted when it starts.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: GAD65 antibodies are present in most patients with type 1 diabetes, usually at lower titres; a titre this high is typical of GAD-associated neurological syndromes, but stiff-person syndrome needs axial rigidity and spasms, which she does not have. The AChR antibody titre and the RNS decrement establish MG.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Pursue stiff-person syndrome workup; miss MG diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).
AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).

findings.description: Residual thymic tissue with fatty involution appropriate for age 45; no discrete mass, nodule or abnormal enhancement.
Lungs clear; no pleural effusion or nodularity.

body_imaging.impression: 1. No anterior mediastinal mass; fatty thymic involution appropriate for age, no thymoma. 2. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear.

interactions: PYRIDOSTIGMINE + INSULIN ASPART or VITAMIN D3: no clinically significant interaction.
PREDNISONE + INSULIN: corticosteroids raise blood glucose, mainly in the afternoon and evening. Moderate. Insulin requirements rise; frequent glucose monitoring and pump rate adjustment needed.
pyridostigmine.proposed: pyridostigmine and prednisone; current medications insulin aspart by subcutaneous pump, vitamin D3 1000 IU; intolerance: codeine (nausea)
warnings: Codeine intolerance (nausea) documented: avoid codeine. Opioids depress respiration and should be used with caution in myasthenia gravis.
Pyridostigmine commonly causes nausea, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea; start at a low dose.

abnormal_values_summary: AChR binding antibody 5.8 nmol/L (H; reference <= 0.02 nmol/L)
labs.interpretation: AChR binding antibody elevated at 5.8 nmol/L, with elevated blocking (58%) and modulating (74%) antibodies. Anti-GAD65 antibody markedly elevated (> 2000 IU/mL). Random glucose 142 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.6% elevated. TSH, free T4 and anti-TPO within reference ranges. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in most patients with generalized autoimmune myasthenia; high-titre GAD65 antibodies occur in type 1 diabetes and in GAD-associated neurological syndromes. Clinical correlation recommended.

specialized_test.impression: Abnormal RNS: 3 Hz decrement in deltoid 17% and nasalis 20% with normal baseline CMAP amplitudes and no post-exercise facilitation (3%). Normal nerve conduction studies. Findings are consistent with a postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission. Clinical correlation recommended.

patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral ptosis, diplopia, and swallowing difficulty for 10 weeks

past_medical_history: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (well controlled on insulin pump)
No prior neuromuscular or autoimmune disease besides DM1

patient.history_present_illness: A 45-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes mellitus managed with an insulin pump presented with 10 weeks of bilateral ptosis, diplopia, and dysphagia. She works as a pharmacist and described noticing her right eyelid drooping approximately 10 weeks ago. She recognized the diurnal variation (consistently worse at the end of her 10-hour pharmacy shifts, better after a night's sleep) as potentially significant. She developed horizontal double vision on looking to the left approximately 7 weeks ago, with the images side by side and worsening with sustained left lateral gaze. She has had difficulty swallowing pills over the past 4 weeks — she has to swallow each pill separately with a large quantity of water and cannot take the multiple tablets she used to take all at once. She reports that her voice becomes nasal and that patients at the pharmacy have commented that her speech sounds different in the afternoon. She has had proximal arm weakness — she asked her colleague to help her reach upper pharmacy shelves because her arms tire out overhead. She denies sensory symptoms, no headache, no neck pain, no limb weakness at rest. Her type 1 diabetes is very well controlled with her insulin pump (HbA1c 6.6%). Her primary care physician referred her urgently to neurology. Her family history includes paternal type 1 diabetes; she was not aware of MG in her family. She has not had any recent infections, new medications, or stressful events beyond her normal busy work schedule.

neurological_exam.additional: Voice nasal after 3 minutes speech. Mild dysphagia — pills difficult to swallow. No respiratory distress.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral ptosis, right greater than left. MRD1 right 0.5 mm, left 3 mm. Complete fatigable ptosis right eye on sustained upgaze at 38 seconds. Horizontal diplopia on leftward gaze. Right eye adduction weakness. Pupils equal, reactive. No proptosis. Facial weakness bilateral.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented. Normal cognition and language.
neurological_exam.motor: Deltoids 4-/5. Hip flexors 4/5. Neck flexors 4-/5. Distal 5/5. Clear fatigability on sustained arm elevation and neck flexion. No axial or limb rigidity, no spasms, normal startle.

physical_exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender; no paraspinal or abdominal wall rigidity.
physical_exam.cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs.
physical_exam.general: Alert, well-appearing woman; bilateral ptosis, right greater than left. Weight 54.8 kg, height 160 cm. Insulin pump in place.
physical_exam.respiratory: Clear to auscultation; no accessory muscle use; SpO2 99% on room air.
